solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Triumphantly show off plate of health food

parts.note: bran is the fibre-rich husk sold as health food
a dish is a plate to serve food on

explanation.surface: Someone proudly holding up a plate of wholesome food for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave something about in a showy, triumphant display.

clue.text: Cricketer out in the middle: Robin helped him

indicators.note: the central letter of the word goes out, dropping the S

parts.note: a batsman is a cricketer who bats

explanation.surface: A cricketer dismissed out on the pitch, with a helper called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The middle' is also the cricket pitch, so 'out in the middle' reads as a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is the sidekick of the masked crusader of Gotham City in DC comics.

clue.text: Roman general is a grand and outstanding person, some say

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: signals a pronunciation, a non-rhotic way of saying the word

parts.note: ripper is old slang for an excellent person or thing

explanation.surface: Praising a Roman commander as a fine and distinguished figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent the final R of RIPPER drops, giving the sound RIPPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman commander who won the battle of Actium for Augustus.

clue.text: A series of cases, nine closed after review

indicators.note: after reviewing, the letters are revised into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: A court winding up nine cases after looking them over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests law, but here they are grammatical cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A declension is the set of inflected forms of a noun across grammatical cases.

clue.text: Stinging insult?

parts.note: a literal stinging blow that is also a figurative affront

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a humiliating rebuff, and the literal version stings the cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an affront or rejection, while literally it is a smack across someone's cheek.

clue.text: In truth, male is hairless

indicators.note: the male letter is placed in the word for truth, so 'In' signals insertion here

parts.note: sooth is an archaic word for truth, as in soothsayer

explanation.surface: A frank observation that some man has no hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth chin or skin is one without stubble or bristles.

clue.text: Oliver wanted this mushroom, not large

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the large letter out

parts.note: a morel is an edible mushroom
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Oliver asked for a mushroom, but not a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Oliver Twist, the hungry orphan asks for more gruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist famously holds out his bowl asking for a further helping.

clue.text: Having continuing success entered into register

definitions.meaning: first meaning: enjoying a winning streak
second meaning: recorded ..., a list of names

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a run of luck also reads literally as being on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is an official list, and being on a roll idiomatically means enjoying a streak of wins.

clue.text: Maybe involved in car accident, so tried

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bash is a minor crash
second meaning: to have a bash is to have a go

explanation.walkthrough: 'So' links the second definition: someone who tried had a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is both a dent from a collision and informal British slang for an attempt.

clue.text: Get away from where the guns are pointing, Jack

indicators.note: says the word get goes away from the longer word, leaving its remainder

parts.note: guns are aimed at a target
the word get is taken as written

explanation.surface: An urgent warning to a sailor to dodge the line of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away' reads as an order to flee, but 'Get' is the letters removed from TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack and tar are both old nicknames for a sailor.

clue.text: Cleaner in African country receiving medal: room excellent!

indicators.note: the country takes in the other pieces, so receiving signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa
an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
A1 (written AI) means first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone in Africa gets an award, and is pleased with their excellent room.
explanation.definitionFit: A chambermaid is a hotel worker who tidies and cleans the bedrooms.

clue.text: Carbon dating erroneous about English plants here

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the E
erroneous letters are wrong and so jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: A scientist doubts radiocarbon results on English plant samples.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanic garden is a place where a wide range of plants are grown for study and display.

clue.text: Realise software I create is hacked

parts.note: an app is a piece of software

indicators.note: hacked suggests the letters are cut about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: A programmer discovers their own creation has been broken into.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate something is to understand or recognise it fully, as in realising its significance.

clue.text: Last home custom-built? Not so much

indicators.note: says only a part of the word is wanted, not all of it

parts.note: the letters sit inside this hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a final resting place could be built to order.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a grave or vault, the final resting place of the dead.

clue.text: College representative broadcast without distortion

parts.note: uni is short for university
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
aired means broadcast on radio or TV

explanation.surface: A college's representative was put on air with crystal-clear sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpaired means undamaged or intact, with nothing weakened or warped.

clue.text: All the lawyers in the county booked

parts.note: the Bar is the legal profession of barristers collectively
set, as in arranged or fixed, a date being booked

explanation.surface: Every lawyer in the county has a full diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Barset is Barsetshire, the fictional English county of Anthony Trollope's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsetshire, shortened to Barset, is Trollope's invented county setting for his Chronicles.

clue.text: Confuse students about working at public library originally

indicators.note: the union letters go about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of these words

parts.note: its two words supply their initial letters

explanation.surface: Students bewildered at what's going on at the local library.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex or baffle them so they don't know how to react.

clue.text: Odd number, grammatically

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the grammatical number for one item

explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd number' reads as one phrase, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means peculiar, and grammatically it is the number contrasting with plural.

clue.text: Beg to have one extra place reserved

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the abbreviation is held back inside the word for extra, kept in reserve there

parts.note: more means extra, additional
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone pleading to have an extra seat booked for them.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead earnestly, the same urgent request as begging.

clue.text: Jumped in after taking a breather during exercise. Then departs

indicators.note: the breathing organ sits during, within, the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education
a lung is an organ one breathes with
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone dived in after a rest during a workout, then leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest; here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive or throw oneself headlong into water.

clue.text: Space traveller needs oxygen to revive

parts.note: a comet travels through space
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An astronaut needing an oxygen supply to come round.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, the phrasal-verb sense of reviving.

clue.text: Kill escort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to take someone out on a date

explanation.walkthrough: Two very different senses of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to assassinate someone and to accompany them on an outing.

clue.text: Mean, I am likely to pocket a note

indicators.note: the note goes into the pocket of the other letters

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be likely to
N is short for note

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they're prone to keeping cash for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to have in mind or plan, which is what mean signifies as a verb.

clue.text: A caterpillar is something to eat

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both the larva and the food it might be mistaken for.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is both a soft-bodied larva and informal slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Mad relatives: one may floor the unwary

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Crazy family members who knock unsuspecting people over.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping on a discarded peel is the classic comic pratfall that sends the careless sprawling.

clue.text: Too stupid at first to enter even parts of Balliol

indicators.note: the initial letter goes inside the even letters
the even letters, second, fourth and sixth, are picked

parts.note: an Oxford college, whose even-placed letters are taken

indicators.note: at first indicates the opening letter

parts.note: its initial letter is used

explanation.surface: A dim student trying to get into an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both meaning in addition.

clue.text: Change round the finale on stage: one has to accept it

indicators.note: in an across clue the second part sits on, following, the first

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: the word for change goes round the word for finale

parts.note: to alter is to change
the end is the finale

explanation.surface: A theatrical director reworks the stage ending of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On stage' reads as theatre, but LEG is a stage of a journey and comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency that a creditor is obliged by law to accept in payment.

clue.text: Reportedly succeeded me formally

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than spelt as it sounds

parts.note: won means came out on top

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone triumphed in place of the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: In formal English the pronoun one stands in for the speaker, as in 'one does one's best'.

clue.text: Wield the rod, extremely passionate

indicators.note: wielding the letters swings them about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: An angler or disciplinarian brandishing a rod with fierce zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot describes intense feeling, burning with fervour.

clue.text: Not prepared to go out as one press chief enters

indicators.note: the editor goes into the word for together

parts.note: united means acting together as one
ED is short for editor, head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's staff stand together when their editor walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy that has not been edited is unready for publication, not yet fit to go out.
